report_name: Warren Criticizes Fed, FDIC, OCC on Weaker Cyber Enforcement

identities.name: Elizabeth Warren
identities.description: U.S. Senator who sent letters to the Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC, criticizing their recent policy changes that she argues weaken cybersecurity enforcement for the banking sector.

identities.name: Federal Reserve
identities.description: A U.S. financial regulator criticized by Senator Warren for implementing a new, narrower definition of 'unsafe or unsound' practices, which she argues weakens cybersecurity oversight.

identities.name: Federal Deposit Insurance Corp.
identities.description: A U.S. financial regulator, also known as the FDIC, criticized by Senator Warren for policy changes that raise the bar for taking enforcement action on cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

identities.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
identities.description: A U.S. financial regulator, also known as the OCC, criticized by Senator Warren for weakening its ability to enforce cybersecurity standards on banks.

identities.name: U.S. Banking System
identities.description: The collective of U.S. financial institutions that Senator Warren warns is being left vulnerable to cyberattacks, particularly from AI-enabled threats, due to weakened regulatory policies.

identities.name: Texas Bankers Association
identities.description: An association whose survey was cited by Senator Warren, showing that 76% of banks have experienced an increase in cyberattacks, highlighting the growing threat landscape.

relationships.source_name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
